title: Trace context enrichment guidelines and metrics bridge
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact working guide to standardize minimal trace context enrichment in the inference runtime and to define a small, stable mapping from trace attributes -> metric anchors -> dashboard widgets. The goal is: make production debugging fast, make SLI computation and alerting deterministic, and bound observability query cost.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to serving-runtime and request-path spans for tokenized inference (hosted, dedicated, and private).
- Minimal set of attributes only: add where cheap to capture; prefer enums/ids to free text.
- Sampling & retention tradeoffs: traces must contain enough metadata to reconstruct root causes without exploding storage.
- This doc is a living checklist (draft) — we expect follow-up refinements after a small pilot.

Design decisions (summary):
1) Always capture a canonical request_id (UUID) on root span and propagate to child spans.
2) Keep tenant and route identifiers short (tenant_id, route_hash) rather than full tenant name.
3) Use discrete codified attributes for runtime state: model_variant, quantization_profile, kernel_path, gpu_type, fallback_tier.
4) Preserve cost-relevant attributes for post-hoc chargebacks: token_count, decode_batch_size, kv_cache_hit (bool), prefix_cache_hit_percent (0-100).
5) Tracing should enrich metrics (not replace them): each critical span will set a small set of attributes that are then rolled up into counter/hist aggregator labels.

Minimum trace attribute set (required on root span):
- request_id: string (uuid)
- timestamp_iso: string
- tenant_id: string (short)
- route_hash: string (short)
- model_variant: string (e.g., gptx-7b-q4)
- seq_len: integer (input_length + expected_output_length)
- token_count: integer (generated tokens)
- kv_cache_hit: boolean (true if prefix cache used)
- batching_key: string (if using batching routing)
- fallback_reason: string|null (e.g., overloaded, kernel-mismatch, cold-start)

Span naming & attributes (examples):
- span.name = "request.root" -> root attributes above
- span.name = "model.decode" -> attributes: model_variant, decode_batch_size (int), kernel_path, gpu_type, gpu_pstate
- span.name = "cache.kv_lookup" -> attributes: kv_cache_hit (bool), lookup_ms (float), keys_examined (int)
- span.name = "router.selection" -> attributes: route_hash, selected_pool, queued_ms
- span.name = "fallback.swap" -> attributes: fallback_from, fallback_to, fallback_reason

Mapping: trace attrs -> metric anchors (recommended label set):
We recommend a small canonical set of labels for high-cardinality-sensitive metrics. For any metric emitted from a span, attach at most these labels: tenant_id, model_variant, route_hash, kv_cache_hit. If the metric is cost-related (token or gpu), also attach seq_len_bucket and batch_size_bucket.

Suggested label buckets (to reduce cardinality):
- seq_len_bucket: small|medium|long (0-128,129-512,>512)
- batch_size_bucket: solo|micro|bulk (1, 2-8, >8)

Metric definitions (starter set):
- inference.request.count: counter by labels [tenant_id, model_variant, route_hash] -> increment on root completion
- inference.request.latency_ms: histogram (use quantiles for dashboard) by [model_variant, seq_len_bucket]
- model.decode.tokens_generated: counter by [model_variant, seq_len_bucket, kv_cache_hit] -> increment by token_count
- kv.lookup.latency_ms: histogram by [kv_cache_hit]
- fallback.swap.count: counter by [fallback_reason, model_variant]
- cost.estimated_gpu_ms: gauge computed at end of request by summing kernel execution durations; label by [model_variant, gpu_type]

Dashboard implications and panel recipes (cost-aware):
- Keep an always-on compact panel: request rate (1m), p50/p90 latency, token rate per second. Labels: model_variant. This is the operator quick-look.
- Cost panel (daily): estimated GPU-ms / tenant_id for last 24h (roll up by model_variant). Use aggregation windows to avoid heavy queries.
- Cold-cache detector: request latency delta between kv_cache_hit=true vs false, plotted by seq_len_bucket.
- Fallback heatmap: matrix with fallback_reason on Y, model_variant on X; cell shows count and p95 latency.
- Query cost guardrails: a dashboard that flags panels with >5s query runtime or >1M series scanned. Mark these as "heavy" with a per-panel cost note.

Tracing sampling & retention strategy (proposal):
1) Head-sample 5% of all traces for full retention (30d) for debugging.
2) Target-sample 100% of traces for root-sample-only (metadata + logs, no full span payload) for 7d.
3) Exception-sample 100%: any trace that triggers fallback_reason or high-latency p95 threshold captured in full regardless of head-sample.
4) On-demand capture: provide an API to temporarily raise sample rate for a tenant or route for investigation.

Instrumentation notes for runtime engineers (practical):
- Where to add attributes: in request ingress handler (tenant_id, route_hash, request_id), in router (selected_pool, queued_ms), in executor (kernel_path, gpu_type, decode_batch_size), in cache layer (kv_cache_hit, lookup_ms).
- Keep attribute values short and stable (avoid embedding user prompts, full model configs, or raw request bodies).
- Use code helpers to set enum-like attributes (e.g., TraceAttr.set("kv_cache_hit", TraceAttr.Bool.TRUE)) to ensure consistent naming.

Example trace annotation snippet (text):
-- root span attrs --
request_id: 5f2e1a6a-...
tenant_id: acct-42
route_hash: r234
model_variant: redwood-7b-q4
seq_len: 256
token_count: 38
kv_cache_hit: false
fallback_reason: null

Open questions and tradeoffs (for next sync):
- How to encode model version stability vs model_variant (we want both but model_version increases cardinality). Option: expose model_version only on sampled traces and use model_variant for metrics.
- Should prefix_cache_hit_percent be stored as integer label or a numeric gauge? Storing as a label increases cardinality but helps immediate filtering.
- Exact thresholds for seq_len_bucket and batch_size_bucket — need workload profiling to finalize.
- How to budget trace storage costs across hosted vs private customers — do we strip attributes automatically for private deployments?

Pilot plan (30d):
Week 0-1: implement root span attr set + router and cache spans; emit metric anchors.
Week 2: add model.decode attributes and cost. Roll out to 10% of traffic on staging.
Week 3: collect dashboards, run operator tabletop for cost queries and latency investigations.
Week 4: iterate on buckets and sampling; finalize instrumentation helpers and docs.

Checklist before wide rollout:
- [ ] SDK helpers for setting canonical attributes (Python/Go/Node).
- [ ] Dashboards for operator quick-look and cost guardrails created and validated.
- [ ] Sampling policy implemented in tracer and configurable via console.
- [ ] Performance test to ensure span annotations add <0.5% P99 latency overhead.

Quick notes to reviewers:
- This doc tries to balance debugging fidelity with cardinality and query cost. If you think we should capture any additional attribute for immediate investigative value (e.g., compile_kernels set), call it out but expect we'll sample it.
- If you are an infra owner and want to run the pilot for a particular pool or tenant, add a comment below with target date.

Action items (owners):
- Priya/Rao: finalize trace attr enum list and open the tracer PR (due 2024-12-05).
- Ethan Kim: prototype dashboard widgets and include query cost notes (due 2024-12-12).
- Lara Chen: run a storage-cost estimate for 1%, 5%, 20% full-trace sampling (due 2024-12-08).
- Samir Patel: validate SDK helpers on a demo client (due 2024-12-18).

Appendix: quick glossary
- metric anchor: the minimal set of labels we attach to metrics so they can be correlated back to traces without exploding cardinality.
- root-sample-only: capture minimal trace metadata and logs but omit verbose span payloads and large buffers.
- fallback_reason: small enum listing the cause for fallback logic (e.g., resource_pressure, model_unavailable, kernel_error, routing_timeout).

Notes-to-self and loose thoughts (raw):
- maybe add a "route_tier" label for premium vs free customers — helps cost-alloc but increases cardinality; maybe derive at aggregation time instead.
- if we can compute estimated GPU-ms cheaply from kernel timers, include it as a label for cost panels but keep raw timers in trace payload for in-depth digs.
- consider auto-trimming long attribute strings in private deployments to reduce PII risk.

-- end --
